findingDetails.title: A 2> or &> redirect target that names a command document still counts as a start
findingDetails.claim: The redirect guard only recognizes a word that starts with >, so a 2> or &> redirect target that ends in .md, .yaml or .yml is pushed as a shell read target and, through readDocument, counts as a start.
findingDetails.evidence: shellReadTargets at :675-681 sets redirect only for words starting with >. readDocument at :922 treats any accepted shell target that tails a command document as a start.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: Checked whether the shell split separates 2> or &> into a token the guard sees; it does not. Checked whether any caller filters the target before readDocument; it does not.
findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: A command could genuinely read the document before the redirect, but the cited case uses head with no file operand, so the document is only the stderr target.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: Withdraw if 2> and &> are declared outside the parser's supported shell grammar, or if a later guard rejects a target that follows a redirect operator.
findingDetails.case: head -n 1 2> .skilled/commands/create/readme.md then a Write; shellReadTargets returns the document path, readDocument returns true, and startState.started is true although the command read stdin and only wrote stderr to the document.
findingDetails.scopeProof: score-command-transcripts.mjs is a named verification surface in the 4c brief; the shell branch at :922 is the T009 fix under check and :677 is the redirect guard it relies on.

searchLedger.hypothesis: A redirect target after 2> or &> is treated as a read target and can start a command.

searchActions.result: The redirect flag is set only for a word starting with >; 2> and &> fall through and their target reaches the .md test.
The accepted target is consumed directly by readDocument, so a false target becomes a false start.
